summary: Multi-part technical analysis by an engineer arguing that GameStop's stock price has been controlled by a high-frequency trading algorithm since 2002. Uses statistical analysis of OHLC data, volume patterns, and historical price comparisons to claim open/close prices are deliberately constrained and that abnormal $0.25 multiple frequencies indicate algorithmic manipulation. Predicts mini-squeezes based on Fibonacci sequences and dividend patterns. Argues retail investors have minimal influence due to algorithmic dominance and implies an eventual MOASS. Analysis is presented as ongoing research with limited definitive proof.

key_claims.claim: Claims that a single high-frequency trading algorithm has controlled GameStop's stock price since late 2002-2003
key_claims.note: No regulatory evidence supports this specific claim; author acknowledges ongoing theorizing without definitive proof (p. 45, 55)

key_claims.claim: Claims that opening and closing prices are deliberately constrained to hit specific price points while high/low values respond to volume
key_claims.note: Alternative explanations (bid-ask spread dynamics, market-making mechanics, order routing) are not addressed; confuses correlation with causation (p. 70-92)

key_claims.claim: Claims that OHLC values ending in $0.25 multiples occur with abnormally high frequency in 2002-2003 and 2021, indicating market fuckery
key_claims.note: Statistical frequency is documented (21% of 1,552 occurrences); however, causality to deliberate manipulation is unproven and could reflect natural rounding (p. 99-129)

key_claims.claim: Claims that a mini squeeze would occur on November 23, 2021, based on Fibonacci sequences and algorithmic patterns
key_claims.note: Book published 2021-11-18; prediction was 5 days out. GME closed ~$172 on Nov 23, 2021 with no notable squeeze; hindsight shows no such event (p. 46)

key_claims.claim: Claims that all 2021 GameStop price data has been predetermined/prewritten by algorithmic control based on historical pattern templates
key_claims.note: Unfalsifiable and presented as theorizing; author acknowledges lack of definitive proof; no causal mechanism demonstrated (p. 150-165)

key_claims.claim: Claims that GameStop will eventually experience a MOASS (Mother of All Short Squeezes) with prices reaching extreme heights
key_claims.note: Implicit throughout ('moon,' 'diamond hands'); hindsight through mid-2026 shows GME peaked at ~$483 intraday Jan 2021, never approached thousands per share

validity_rationale: The core thesis—that a specific algorithmic script controls GME—is not substantiated by credible evidence and rests on inferential leaps from statistical patterns. The key near-term prediction (Nov 23, 2021 squeeze) failed outright. The MOASS prediction is contradicted by hindsight (no such event through 2026). While the author uses real market data and legitimate statistical techniques, the interpretation conflates correlation with causation, cherry-picks historical date comparisons, and treats speculation as conclusion. The author acknowledges being mid-analysis and lacking definitive proof.
